We have theoretically investigated the effects of a random discrete distribution of implanted and annealed arsenic (As) atoms on the device characteristics of silicon nanowire (Si NW) transistors.

To achieve this, we utilized Kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) simulation to generate realistic random distributions of active As atoms within Si NWs. These active As distributions were then introduced into the source and drain extensions of n-type gate-all-around NW transistors.

RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) are implicated in these diverse aspects, as hundreds of RBPs are encoded in eukaryotic genomes. ### The Choice Between Friction and Fragility

**Option (a): The Drawback of Input**
When users are forced to manually enter a username before accessing your app, you immediately undermine its core appeal. Furthermore, there is no guarantee that the username you request will be unique. This approach introduces unnecessary friction and introduces the risk of duplicate accounts.

**Option (b): The Power of Seamless Recall**
This is the far less onerous option for the user, offering the superior experience of automatic login without manual entry. However, it introduces a critical limitation: it only allows you to remember the user on a single device. Consider the frustration of a user upgrading to a brand-new device. With this approach, they would face the inevitable disconnect, only to find that your app no longer recognizes their account.

**Choose the path that guarantees a seamless, persistent experience for every user, every device.**

Option (a) is problematic. First, asking the user to type something before entering your app will automatically make your app less appealing. Second, there's no guarantee that the username chosen will be unique. Option (b) is less onerous for the user, but it's tricky to get right. More importantly, it only allows you to remember the user on one device. Imagine the frustration of someone who upgrades to a shiny new device, only to find that your app no longer remembers them.

This paper presents a suitable numerical wave model based on the Boussinesq-Wave-Equations (BWE), which extend the theory to simulate the influence of currents on waves and nonlinear wave-wave interactions within a propagating spectrum. An analytical approach to wave-current interaction was previously provided by Longuet-Higgins and Steward (1960) [3], who studied linear small-amplitude waves in moving media and introduced radiation stress to determine changes in wavelength and amplitude based on current speed and wave direction; their foundational work later served as a basis for models reviewed by Jonsson (1989) [2]. While many existing models are limited to linear theory, the BWE is necessary to model weakly nonlinear waves in shallow water where bottom topography significantly influences the wave climate, a condition that linear theory cannot describe. This modeling approach originated in the late 1970s and has been validated through numerous studies, demonstrating accurate simulation of combined refraction, diffraction, reflection, and shoaling (e.g., Madsen and Warren, 1984 [4]) as well as nonlinear wave-wave interactions over uneven beds (e.g., Priiser, Schaper, and Zielke, 1986 [7]). Ultimately, Boussinesq wave models have evolved into a practical tool essential for engineering applications.

Hypotension is strongly associated with poor patient outcomes. Consequently, reversing this condition must be a primary therapeutic goal in the early stages of shock. Potent inotropic and vasoconstrictor agents are de rigueur in the treatment of shock. Our therapeutic goal is to maintain the mean arterial pressure (MAP) at levels above 60 mmHg, a value thought to be the minimal pressure head required for coronary and renal perfusion [1].

Should we aim for higher, or perhaps even lower, MAP values?

The decision-making process is complicated by the dual nature of catecholamines. In septic shock, the balance between the positive and negative effects of vasopressor and inotropic agents is even more difficult to discern [3].

Subject: The Evolution of Book Cover Design

Dear Valued Customer,

I hope this message finds you well.

Inspired by rising literacy rates and advancing technologies, the nineteenth century saw the book transform from a largely hand-made object to a mass-produced product. In this new context, a book's cover took on added importance: it was no longer merely a functional protection for the pages but instead a key platform through which to communicate and sell the book.

Prior to this, covers had — bar a smattering of highly bespoke one-off creations (e.g. embroidered covers for personal libraries) — mostly been plain leather bound affairs. From the 1820s, with the rise of mechanical bookbinding, these leather covers of old gave way to new cloth coverings — known as publisher's bindings — which, in addition to being inexpensive, were now also printable. A wide variety of cover printing techniques were employed over the decades: from embossing to gilt to multi-colour lithography. An entirely new artistic space was opened up. It was one in which illustrators and designers thrived, producing a range of covers as eclectic in aesthetic approach as the myriad contents they fronted.

From around the 1920s, the paper dust jacket — previously there to simply protect the publisher's binding — began to sport designs (and, of course, then paperbacks), but it was in the hundred years preceding, on these printed cloths, that book cover design first truly flourished.

Thank you for your continued trust in our work.

Best regards,

**Marshaled by Value (MBV):**

This model was calibrated using various in situ and airborne data sources. This model was calibrated using various sources of in situ and airborne data. In the present study, we propose to evaluate the L-MEB model on the basis of a large set of airborne data, recorded by the CAROLS radiometer during the course of 20 flights made over South West France (the SMOSMANIA site), and supported by simultaneous soil moisture measurements, made in 2009 and 2010. In terms of volumetric soil moisture, the retrieval accuracy achieved with the L-MEB model, with two default roughness parameters, ranges between 8% and 13%. Local calibrations of the roughness parameter, using data from the 2009 flights for different areas of the site, allowed an accuracy of approximately 5.3% to be achieved with the 2010 CAROLS data. Simultaneously we estimated the vegetation optical thickness (t) and we showed that, when roughness is locally adjusted, MODIS NDVI values are correlated (R2 = 0.36) to t. Finally, as a consequence of the significant influence of the roughness parameter on the estimated absolute values of soil moisture, we propose to evaluate the relative variability of the soil moisture, using a default soil roughness parameter. The soil moisture variations are estimated with an uncertainty of approximately 6%.

**Case Profile:** A 49-year-old male patient presents with a complex cardiac emergency involving prosthetic mitral valve endocarditis, severe QT prolongation, and life-threatening arrhythmias.

**The Incident:** Asymptomatic for over a year, this patient was admitted to our emergency unit in January 2012 with a triad of syncope, fever, and suspicion of endocarditis. Comprehensive cardiologic workup, including transthoracic (TTE) and transesophageal (TEE) echocardiograms, confirmed vegetations on the prosthetic mitral valve. Microbiological analysis revealed positive cultures for *Methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus*.

**The Crisis:** Upon admission, the patient exhibited a markedly prolonged corrected QT (QTc) interval of **540 ms**. During this period, he experienced multiple episodes of **torsades de pointes (TdP)**, a life-threatening arrhythmia. Fortunately, he was successfully recovered following bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR).

**The Resolution:** Remarkably, the clinical course was fully normalized **4 weeks** after the initial admission. The profound QT prolongation and characteristic deep inverted T wave completely resolved. The patient subsequently completed a 45-day course of triple antibiotic therapy, achieving a successful clinical outcome.

**Discussion:** This case serves as a critical study on the mechanisms of QT prolongation in the setting of acute infection and inflammation. We discuss the specific pathophysiological factors driving QT prolongation in this patient, offering vital insights into the interplay between *S. aureus* infection and cardiac electrical stability.

### The Two Worlds of Sedimentation

While sedimentation in the fjords is primarily driven by river/meltwater discharge and coastal erosion by sea ice/glaciers—resulting in high supplies of terrigenous organic matter—the environment on the outer shelf and slope is characterized by Atlantic water inflow, which significantly enhances marine organic matter supply.

In the fjords, local deviations from this pattern are explained by erosion and the out-washing of fine-grained material by bottom currents. Conversely, spots dominated by marine productivity, such as those near the island of Spitsbergen, off the Kongsfjord/Krossfjord area, and in the west off Prins Karls Forland, reflect local upwelling of nutrient-rich Atlantic water-derived water masses.

We have uncovered a sobering trend: accumulation rates of marine organic carbon have decreased since the middle of the last century. This decline is reflected in reconstructed primary productivities that have dropped over time, a phenomenon we have meticulously documented in our data.

### The Role of Global Warming

Our analysis exposes a fascinating, yet alarming, correlation between temperature and productivity. The negative relationship between the Isfjord temperature record and reconstructed productivities in the Storfjord is explained by a reduced annual duration of the marginal ice zone (MIJ). The Storfjord area stands out as an extreme case of this phenomenon. Our findings indicate that extremely high accumulation rates of marine organic carbon—marked between **5.4 and 17.2 g/m²/yr**—mark the Storfjord area and likely high-latitude fjord environments in general as the Barents Sea's primary sink for carbon dioxide.

Abstract: Solar ultraviolet (UV) radiation is widely known as a genotoxic environmental agent that affects Earth ecosystems and the human population. As a primary consequence of the stratospheric ozone layer depletion observed over the last decades, the increasing UV incidence levels have heightened the concern regarding deleterious consequences affecting both the biosphere and humans, thereby leading to an increase in scientific efforts to understand the role of sunlight in the induction of DNA damage, mutagenesis, and cell death. Apart from the data thus generated, the development of novel biosensors could help in evaluating the biological effects of sunlight on the environment. 🌱 **Can we make eco-taxes more popular? The answer might be in how we present them.**

Ecological (eco) taxes are promising mechanisms to enable eco-friendly decisions, but few people prefer them. In this study, we present a way in which eco-tax options may be communicated to the general public to encourage their payment.

Our implementation, called "**information presentation**," takes advantage of the non-linear relationship between eco-tax payments and CO2 emissions and the human reliance on the **proportional-thinking heuristic**. According to this heuristic, people are likely to prefer a small eco-tax increase and judge larger eco-tax increases to cause proportionally greater CO2 emissions reductions.

In an online study, participants were asked to choose between eco-tax increases in two problems:
✅ In one, a smaller eco-tax increase resulted in greater CO2 emissions reduction.
✅ In the other, a smaller tax increase resulted in lesser CO2 emissions reduction.

**The findings were revealing**:
Although the larger eco-tax increase did not reduce CO2 emissions the most, across both problems, people judged larger eco-tax increases to cause proportionally greater reductions in CO2 emissions and preferred smaller tax increases.

🚀 **The takeaway**: Eco-tax policies would benefit by presenting information in terms of eco-tax increases, such that smaller eco-tax increases (which are more attractive and are likely to be chosen by people) cause greater CO2 emissions reductions.

Here is a friendly overview of how lymph flows through a lymph node: Lymph circulates to the lymph node via afferent lymphatic vessels and drains into the node just beneath the capsule in a space called the subcapsular sinus. From there, the subcapsular sinus drains into trabecular sinuses and finally into medullary sinuses. The sinus space is criss-crossed by the pseudopods of macrophages which act to trap foreign particles and filter the lymph. The medullary sinuses converge at the hilum and lymph then leaves the lymph node via the efferent lymphatic vessel. Additionally, lymphocytes, both B cells and T cells, constantly circulate through the lymph nodes. They enter the lymph node via the bloodstream and cross the wall of blood vessels by the process of diapedesis.

Additionally, patients may retain these bodies following radiation therapy targeting the spleen, such as the treatment for Hodgkin lymphoma.

Understanding these findings is vital for accurate diagnosis and management of underlying hematological conditions.

# Decoding the Blueprint of Development: How Embryonic Tissue Origins Shape Gene Expression Patterns

Our groundbreaking study maps human and mouse tissues onto the definitive mammalian fate map of embryogenesis, revealing critical insights into how developmental origins dictate molecular identity. By integrating individual gene expression data with Gene Ontology (GO) analysis, we validate a pivotal hypothesis: tissues originating from the same embryonic segments share significantly more similarity in their gene expression profiles than those from remote, divergent branches of the fate map.

**The Fate Map Reveal**
Our data confirms this evolutionary pattern is most pronounced in **ectoderm** and **mesoderm**, where tissues from the same embryonic segments exhibit greater expression conservation than those from different origins. However, a distinct exception exists in **endoderm**, where tissues from the same segments often diverge more than tissues from remote branches.

**The Molecular Mechanism**
The divergence in endoderm is likely driven by **gene imprinting**, a process where tissues inherit molecular traits from their ancestors throughout development. This epigenetic mechanism, involving **DNA methylation**, **histone modification**, and other epigenetic factors, ensures conservation of gene expression in neighboring tissues while causing divergence in distant segments. Furthermore, expression divergence varies greatly across different sub-groups of the fate map.

**Key Findings**
*   **Neural Tissues (Ectoderm):** These represent the most conserved sub-group. Their genes show greater similarity than mesoderm-derived tissues, featuring more conserved individual genes, more conserved GO modules, and significantly more correlated GO modules.
*   **Endoderm:** This tissue group displays a large number of differentially expressed genes. This high variability may reflect the distinct functional requirements of these tissues and their prolonged development within the embryo.

*Source: [8]*

In this study, we mapped human and mouse tissues onto the mammalian fate map of embryogenesis and further analyzed the expression conservation of tissues with individual genes and gene set (Gene Ontology) based methods. We tested the hypothesis the tissues from the same branch on the fate map shared more similarity in gene expression profile with each other than their remote neighbors. Our study presents a critical insight into the early dynamics of hemorrhagic shock, though it also highlights important experimental constraints.

**Key Findings & Early Disparities**
Despite the animals receiving extremely large resuscitation volumes—far exceeding typical human clinical scenarios—differences in blood volume (EVLWI) and blood loss manifested very early, prior to exceeding resuscitation volumes typically used in practice.

**The Role of Fluid Type**
Our data indicates that the choice of fluid type, rather than the sheer volume of resuscitation alone, drives these outcomes. As previously established, distinct differences in pH and coagulation between Low-Risk (LR) and Normal Saline (NS) groups occur immediately after the initiation of fluid resuscitation [24]. This confirms that the observed variations in Endovascular Loss of Intravascular Volume Intraosseously and blood loss are fundamentally attributable to fluid composition, not volume alone.

**Study Limitations**
It is important to acknowledge our study's limitations. By study end, the animals had received resuscitation volumes that were exceptionally large, typically exceeding those seen in human clinical scenarios. This reflects both the inherent severity of our model and our deliberate choice to resuscitate to a baseline Mean Arterial Pressure (MAP). Consequently, we observed supranormal urine outputs in the NS group, suggesting resuscitation beyond normal perfusion levels.

**Strategic Rationale**
Despite these volume differences, our rationale for excluding vasoactive medications was sound. We did not utilize vasoactive drugs, despite the large volumes administered, because they are currently rarely used in the early resuscitation of hemorrhagic shock.

**Conclusion**
Our results suggest that fluid type is the primary driver of observed outcomes in this model.

Subject: Update on Our Study of CNGC19 and CNGC20 in Arabidopsis thaliana

Dear Gus,

I hope this message finds you well.

We are pleased to share the results from our recent study using GUS, GFP, and luciferase reporter assays to examine the expression of the CNGC19 and CNGC20 genes from *Arabidopsis thaliana* in response to developmental cues and salt stress.

Here are the key findings:

*   **Tissue-Specific Expression:** Both genes showed differential expression between roots and shoots. The CNGC19 gene was predominantly active in roots from early growth stages, with major expression observed in the phloem. In contrast, CNGC20 showed the highest promoter activity in mesophyll cells surrounding the veins, and its expression increased during development to peak in mature and senescent leaves.
*   **Response to Salt Stress:** While both genes were upregulated in the shoot in response to elevated NaCl concentrations but not mannitol, the responses differed by tissue. In the roots, CNGC19 did not respond to changes in salt concentration; however, in the shoot, it was strongly upregulated within the observed time frame (6–72 hours). Additionally, salt-induction of CNGC20 was observed in the shoot, starting just one hour after stress treatment. These induction patterns occurred with similar kinetics, whether NaCl was applied to the roots of intact plants or to the petiole of detached leaves.
*   **Salt Tolerance and Ion Content:** We measured no differences in potassium (K) and sodium (Na) contents in the shoots of homozygous T-DNA insertion lines for CNGC19 and CNGC20. Notably, these lines developed a growth phenotype in the presence of up to 75 mM NaCl similar to that of the wild type.

Please let us know if you have any questions or would like to discuss these results further.

Best regards,

[Your Name]

Subject: Information about Soft Water and Hard Water

Dear Customer,

Soft water is the term used to describe types of water that contain few or no calcium or magnesium metal cations. This term is usually related to hard water, which does contain significant amounts of these ions.

Soft water typically comes from peat or igneous rock sources, such as granite, but may also derive from sandstone sources, since such sedimentary rocks are usually low in calcium and magnesium.

There are water-softening devices used in households and by industry to remove the hardness-causing minerals from hard water to create artificially soft water. Typically, such devices exchange the calcium and magnesium ions in the hard water for sodium ions (ion exchange), or remove most of the soluble species in the water to produce water with little or no mineral content (de-ionisation).

Please feel free to reach out if you have any further questions regarding water treatment options.

Best regards,

While the term "experiment" typically connotes a controlled experiment, this approach is often impossible when necessary. In such scenarios, researchers employ natural experiments, or quasi-experiments, which depend solely on the observation of variables within the system rather than the manipulation of specific ones. To the greatest extent possible, these studies aim to gather data that isolates the contribution of each variable while holding others constant, thereby allowing researchers to discern the effects of the remaining variables. The reliability of this method hinges on the correlation between explanatory variables in the observed data: when these variables exhibit low correlation, natural experiments approach the power of controlled experiments. However, because natural experiments frequently occur in uncontrolled environments, variables from undetected sources may remain unmeasured or uncontrolled, potentially generating illusory correlations that compromise the study's reliability. Consequently, the degree to which natural experiments approximate the power of controlled experiments is inversely proportional to the correlation between the explanatory variables; the lower the correlation, the higher the potential for valid conclusions, while the higher the correlation, the greater the risk of unreliable results.

The term "experiment" usually implies a controlled experiment, but sometimes controlled experiments are prohibitively difficult or impossible. In this case researchers resort to natural experiments, also called quasi-experiments. Natural experiments rely solely on observations of the variables of the system under study, rather than manipulation of just one or a few variables as occurs in controlled experiments. To the degree possible, they attempt to collect data for the system in such a way that contribution from all variables can be determined, and where the effects of variation in certain variables remain approximately constant so that the effects of other variables can be discerned. The degree to which this is possible depends on the observed correlation between explanatory variables in the observed data. When these variables are not well correlated, natural experiments can approach the power of controlled experiments. Usually, however, there is some correlation between these variables, which reduces the reliability of natural experiments relative to what could be concluded if a controlled experiment were performed. Also, because natural experiments usually take place in uncontrolled environments, variables from undetected sources are neither measured nor held constant, and these may produce illusory correlations in variables under study.

During the last glacial period, sea ice and dust fluxes increased greatly in the Southern Ocean. While palaeorecords offer contradictory evidence regarding marine productivity in this region, data were sparse beyond one glacial cycle; however, we present continuous chemical proxy data spanning the last eight glacial cycles (740,000 years) from the Dome C Antarctic ice core. These data constrain winter sea-ice extent in the Indian Ocean, Southern Ocean biogenic productivity, and Patagonian climatic conditions. We found that maximum sea-ice extent is closely tied to Antarctic temperature on multi-millennial timescales but less so on shorter timescales. Biological dimethylsulphide emissions south of the polar front seem to have changed little with climate, suggesting that sulphur compounds were not active in climate regulation. We observe large glacial-interglacial contrasts in iron deposition, which we infer reflects strongly changing Patagonian conditions. During glacial terminations, changes in Patagonia apparently preceded sea-ice reduction, indicating that multiple mechanisms may be responsible for different phases of CO2 increase during glacial terminations. We also observe no changes in internal climatic feedbacks that could have caused the change in amplitude of Antarctic temperature variations observed 440,000 years ago.
